description: We are Nyx, a young team passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. Some of us are beginners in programming, but we are curious, creative, and eager to learn and solve problems together. We are looking for teammates interested in programming, science, AI, design, research, and communication. We value teamwork, initiative, commitment, and the desire to create something meaningful.
summary:
"Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" is a 3D educational simulator designed for children aged 7 to 12. It allows players to experience the challenges of a mission to Mars by taking on six different crew roles and managing essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy. Through different mission stages, players must make decisions, solve emergencies, and work together to keep the crew safe.

Our project addresses the challenge of making space exploration more interactive and accessible. We use real NASA data and resources, including DONKI, OSDR, and RadLab, to create realistic mission conditions and meaningful challenges.

This project is important because it transforms scientific information into a hands-on learning experience. It encourages critical thinking, teamwork, problem-solving, and resource management while helping children develop an interest in science and space exploration.
details:
Our project, "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer," is aimed at helping students to recognize, learn and experience a space mission through an educational simulator developed with real data from NASA and information from previous missions. It works as a multiplayer game, but during the simulation, students are able to make fast decisions, protect the crew from any problems during the mission, learn about the different safety rules involved in being an astronaut, and work as a team to achieve the mission's goals. Thanks to our easy-to-use interface and voice chat, participants can interact with each other in real time; plus, the language and graphics of this simulator are written in TypeScript, and the interface and the 3D environment were built using Three.js and React Three Fiber. In the case of the simulation, a Cloudflare server calculated oxygen, CO2, water, food, energy, radiation, and each tripulant's health based on NASA sources. Thanks to Cloudflare, each mission has its own small server, and students can interact in real time. The code was developed with the help of AI as a programming assistant. In addition, it is not necessary to download anything or create an account. To start the simulation, students have the facility to just write their names and share the simulation code to access their room if they play in multiplayer.

On the other hand, during the simulation, we considered it important to introduce the students before starting to play, to help them to get familiar with the interface and get ready for the mission through a four-step protocol which includes recognize the mission goals, choose a role, managing suppliers and choosing a difficulty level: Cadet, Astronaut or Commander. Next, during the simulation, notifications will appear to warn tripulants about problems related to supplies, radiation, oxygen, the route direction, tripulants ' health, and so on. Then students will be able to make fast decisions to help the crew.

Moreover, to be more creative, we decided to implement bots when a crew is not complete to offer a close experience of a space team. Also, we added definitions of technical words related to a space mission to introduce students to this field. Besides that, we designed this app so that each decision could have a consequence, to illustrate that, during a mission, turning on the lights comes at a cost—it drains the battery—and rationing food wears out the crew.

This app is available for students from 7 to 12; nevertheless, the learning experience that this project offers is suitable for all ages, because we seek to share the knowledge of a space mission with every student willing to learn. The impact of this project is represented in each student who learns something new and gets inspired to explore the programming and space science field. Access to this educational simulator is totally free and does not require downloading, personal data, or an account.
